title: Book I, Sections I–III — From First and Last Ratios to the Inverse-Square Law
edition: Isaac Newton, The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy, trans. Andrew Motte (1729); Wikisource transcription.

nodes.name: Lemma II
nodes.summary: Inscribed and circumscribed rectangles under a curve have an ultimate ratio of equality.

nodes.name: Lemma III
nodes.summary: The same ultimate equality holds even when the rectangle breadths are unequal.

nodes.name: Lemma IV
nodes.summary: If corresponding parts share an ultimate ratio, the whole figures share it too.

nodes.name: Lemma V
nodes.summary: In similar figures, areas are as the squares of homologous sides.

nodes.name: Lemma VI
nodes.summary: The angle between chord and tangent vanishes as the arc shrinks.

nodes.name: Lemma VII
nodes.summary: Arc, chord, and tangent become ultimately equal as the arc vanishes.

nodes.name: Lemma IX
nodes.summary: Areas of the limiting triangles are in the duplicate ratio of their sides.

nodes.name: Lemma X
nodes.summary: Spaces described from rest under a finite force are as the squares of the times.

nodes.name: Lemma XI
nodes.summary: The evanescent subtense of contact is as the square of the subtense of the arc.

nodes.name: Law I
nodes.summary: A body perseveres in rest or uniform straight motion unless compelled to change.

nodes.name: Law II
nodes.summary: Change of motion is proportional to the impressed force and in its direction.

nodes.name: Prop. I, Theorem I
nodes.summary: Radii to an immovable centre sweep equal areas in equal times (Kepler's 2nd law).

nodes.name: Prop. II, Theorem II
nodes.summary: Conversely, a body sweeping equal areas is urged by a centripetal force to that centre.

nodes.name: Prop. IV, Theorem IV
nodes.summary: In uniform circular motion the centripetal force is as the square of the velocity over the radius.

nodes.name: Prop. VI, Theorem V
nodes.summary: Centripetal force is as the versed sine of the nascent arc directly and the square of the time inversely.

nodes.name: Prop. VII, Problem II
nodes.summary: For a body in a circle with force to any given point, the force is reciprocally as the fifth power of the distance.

nodes.name: Lemma XII
nodes.summary: All parallelograms circumscribed about conjugate diameters of an ellipse are equal.

nodes.name: Prop. XI, Problem VI
nodes.summary: A body in an ellipse with force to the focus is urged by a force reciprocally as the square of the distance.

nodes.name: Prop. XIII, Problem VIII
nodes.summary: A body in a parabola with force to the focus obeys the same inverse-square law.

nodes.name: Prop. XV, Theorem VII
nodes.summary: Periodic times in ellipses are as the 3/2 power of the major axes (Kepler's 3rd law).

edges.label: by the second Law of Motion
